calls.reason: The planning study extracted usable models but required 59 feedback messages to fix 56 factual errors. Its narrow domains and reliance on corrections leave the broader reliability claim unresolved.
Scientific Reports found 18% of GPT-4 citations fabricated under ordinary requests. NewsGuard elicited all 100 false narratives, versus 80 for GPT-3.5, and judged GPT-4's output more convincing.
OpenAI acknowledged fabricated answers, and the moral-advice study found inconsistency. Neither establishes the claimed lack of physical and psychological understanding in the original ChatGPT.
The prediction concerns retrospectives written in 2043. The packet contains no qualifying evidence, and that year remains in the future.
OpenAI's report shows GPT-4 responses preferred on 70.2% of prompts, supporting improved capabilities. It does not establish that remaining errors stem from architecture, whose details were withheld.
The infectious-disease study rated 16% of GPT-4 management plans harmful and only one optimal. The more favorable consultation study still found unmet information needs and hallucinated references.
